reason: Section 23 is a single designation authority allowing the Minister to designate inspectors for the purposes of the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister designation of inspectors

evidenceText: The Minister may designate any person as an inspector for the purposes of this Act

proposedGroups.reason: The target contains one operative authority identifying who may designate inspectors and for what statutory purpose.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the Minister may designate any person as an inspector for the purposes of the Act.

reason: Section 24 is a cohesive inspector-powers provision covering reasonable-time entry with identification, inspection and testing of contaminant-related places and processes, and sampling authority.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Inspector entry, inspection, testing, and sampling powers

evidenceText: at any reasonable time and upon presentation of identification
enter any area, land, place or premises
inspect and test any process of production or manufacture
take samples of any substance or material

proposedGroups.reason: The provision lists the inspector powers available for administering the Act, tied to contaminant-related places, structures, processes, materials, and samples.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when inspectors may enter, inspect, test, and take samples for administering the Act.

reason: Section 24.1 is a focused restriction on inspector entry into private dwellings, with three permitted bases for entry under section 24.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Private dwelling limits on inspector entry

evidenceText: shall not enter a private dwelling under section 24 unless
acting in an emergency situation
has the consent
obtains an entry warrant

proposedGroups.reason: The provision states a prohibition on private-dwelling entry unless emergency, adult occupant consent, or an Entry Warrants Act warrant applies.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the emergency, consent, and entry-warrant bases that allow an inspector to enter a private dwelling under section 24.

reason: Section 24.2 is a single evidence-detention authority for objects, substances, samples, and documentary material discovered by an inspector under section 24 on reasonable grounds.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Inspector detention of evidence discovered under section 24

evidenceText: may detain for the purposes of evidence
any object, substance or material or a sample
any documentary material regardless of physical form or characteristics
believes, on reasonable grounds, may afford evidence

proposedGroups.reason: The provision identifies what an inspector may detain, the evidentiary purpose, and the reasonable-grounds connection to a violation or failure to comply.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what inspectors may detain as evidence after discovering it while acting under section 24.

reason: Section 25 is a focused duty for owners, persons in charge, employees, and agents to assist inspectors and furnish reasonably required information.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Assistance and information duties owed to inspectors

evidenceText: shall give all reasonable assistance to an inspector
to enable the inspector to carry out the inspector’s duties
shall furnish the inspector with such information as the inspector may reasonably require

proposedGroups.reason: The provision contains one assistance-and-information obligation owed by specified persons connected to an area, land, place, or premises.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who must assist inspectors and provide information reasonably required for inspector duties.

reason: Section 26 is a single prohibition against obstructing or hindering inspectors in carrying out their duties under the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Prohibition on obstructing or hindering inspectors

evidenceText: No person shall obstruct or hinder an inspector in the carrying out of the inspector’s duties under this Act

proposedGroups.reason: The target contains one inspector-protection prohibition.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that no person may obstruct or hinder an inspector carrying out duties under the Act.

reason: Section 27 is a single prohibition against knowingly making false or misleading oral or written statements to inspectors or other persons carrying out Act duties.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: False or misleading statements to inspectors

evidenceText: No person shall knowingly, make a false or misleading statement
either orally or in writing
to an inspector or other person engaged in carrying out his duties

proposedGroups.reason: The provision contains one truthfulness obligation for statements made to inspectors or other duty-carrying persons under the Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that knowingly false or misleading oral or written statements to inspectors or other Act-duty persons are prohibited.

reason: Section 28 is a single designation authority allowing the Minister to designate analysts for the purposes of the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister designation of analysts

evidenceText: The Minister may designate any person as an analyst for the purposes of this Act

proposedGroups.reason: The target contains one operative authority identifying who may designate analysts and for what statutory purpose.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the Minister may designate any person as an analyst for the purposes of the Act.

reason: Section 29 is a cohesive evidentiary provision for analyst certificates, including admissibility and proof, cross-examination with leave, and notice before production.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Analyst certificate evidence, cross-examination, and notice
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections work together on how analyst certificates are used in prosecutions and what procedural protections apply to the opposing party.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an analyst certificate is admissible and proof, and how cross-examination and notice requirements apply.

reason: Section 30 is a single payment duty for applicants, persons taking proceedings, and authorization holders to pay regulation-established fees, rentals, and charges in the prescribed manner.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Fees, rentals, and charges payable under regulations

evidenceText: An applicant, a person who takes any proceeding
a holder of a registration, licence, permit or approval
shall pay the fees, rentals and charges established by regulation

proposedGroups.reason: The provision identifies who must pay and ties the amounts and manner of payment to regulation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who must pay fees, rentals, and charges established by regulation and how payment is prescribed.

reason: Section 31 is a single application rule binding both the Crown in right of Canada and the Crown in right of the Province to the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Crown bound by the Clean Environment Act

evidenceText: The Crown in right of Canada and the Crown in right of the Province are bound by the provisions of this Act

proposedGroups.reason: The target contains one rule identifying the Crown entities bound by the Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that both the federal and provincial Crown are bound by the Act.

reason: Section 31.1 is a large environmental-impact-assessment regulation provision with distinct topics for definitions, regulation powers over designation and assessment process, enforcement and administration powers, and application or exemption rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Environmental impact assessment definitions
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 31.1(1) defines the key terms that govern the environmental-impact-assessment regulation powers in the rest of the section.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the section 31.1 meanings of environment, environmental impact, environmental impact assessment, proponent, and undertaking.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulation powers for undertaking designation, registration, assessment, and public process
proposedGroups.reason: The first part of subsection 31.1(2) authorizes regulations for designating undertakings, registration and re-registration, assessment classification, assessment work, reports, review committees, public access to reports and statements, public meetings, determinations, approvals, and criteria.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers that structure undertaking designation, registration, environmental impact assessment, review, reporting, public process, and approval criteria.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulation powers for proponent prohibitions, orders, inspectors, fees, and schedules
proposedGroups.reason: The later part of subsection 31.1(2) authorizes regulations for carrying-on prohibitions, terms and conditions, discontinuance orders, effects of orders, inspector powers, fees, suspension or revocation, and submission of drawings, specifications, information, and schedules.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers for enforcing environmental-impact-assessment requirements through proponent prohibitions, conditions, orders, inspector powers, fees, suspension, revocation, and schedules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Application and exemption rules for environmental regulations
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 31.1(3) through 31.1(5) separately address the general or specific reach of regulations, their temporal application, and the Lieutenant-Governor in Council's exemption power.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how section 31.1 regulations may apply generally or specifically, which undertakings they apply to, and how an undertaking may be exempted.

reason: Section 32 contains many current regulation-making powers even though the supplied content flags mark the target as repeal-only; the operative text supports authoring, but the flag conflict warrants caution.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulation powers for authorizations, fees, appeals, and commissions

evidenceText: prescribing any matter to be waste
respecting the granting of an exemption in relation to a Wetland Designation Order or a Coastal Designation Order
prescribing or authorizing the Minister to establish the form of and the manner
providing for the appeal of any order or decision
respecting additional functions and duties for water or wastewater commissions

proposedGroups.reason: The opening active paragraphs cover waste prescription, designation-order exemptions, authorization forms and processes, fees, appeals, water or wastewater commission functions, voting, annual reports, and section 30 tariffs.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers for waste, designation-order exemptions, authorizations, fees, appeals, and water or wastewater commissions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulation powers for inspectors, ice structures, sources, works, contaminants, and water

evidenceText: respecting the duties and powers of inspectors and analysts
regulating, controlling or prohibiting the erection or placing of structures
construction, alteration, modification, operation, location, repair, monitoring, testing, inspection, discharge or removal
handling, disposal, removal, release, testing, monitoring and treatment
withdrawal, use, storage and handling of water

proposedGroups.reason: These active paragraphs authorize regulations for inspector and analyst duties, samples and analyses, structures on ice, contaminant sources and works, contaminants and waste, and water withdrawal, use, storage, and handling.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers over inspectors and analysts, ice structures, contaminant sources and works, contaminant or waste handling, and water use or storage.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulation powers for approval terms, cost recovery, insurance, security, and claims

evidenceText: terms and conditions upon which registrations, licences, permits and approvals may be refused
responsibility for and the payment and recovery of any costs incurred by the Minister
generally respecting insurance coverage or the posting of security
carriage, conduct and settlement of claims and actions
procedure for the collection of costs incurred by the Minister

proposedGroups.reason: These paragraphs focus on authorization terms and conditions, Minister or other-person cost responsibility and recovery, insurance and security, claims and actions, and cost collection procedures.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers for authorization conditions, cost responsibility and recovery, insurance or security, claims, and Minister cost collection.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulation powers for contaminant measurement, notices, contaminated sites, and site professionals

evidenceText: methods, standards or tests for determining the amount, concentration, level or presence
the circumstances under which a notice shall be given of the release or presence of a contaminant
respecting contaminated sites, including
criteria for assessment, designation, remediation and rehabilitation of contaminated sites
establishing requirements for site professionals

proposedGroups.reason: These paragraphs authorize regulations for measurement standards, release or presence notices, contaminated-site criteria, obligations, reports, remedial measures, agreements, databases, prosecution or administrative-penalty conditions, delegation, and site-professional requirements.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers for contaminant measurement, release notices, contaminated-site management, responsible-party obligations, reports, databases, delegations, and site professionals.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulation powers for stewardship boards and designated materials

evidenceText: respecting the creation and operation of stewardship boards
designating materials for the purposes of section 22.1
respecting the manufacture, importation, distribution, sale, supply
registrations and licences in relation to the management of designated materials
designated material stewardship plans

proposedGroups.reason: The stewardship-board and designated-material paragraphs authorize regulations for board creation and operation, material designation, material handling, advertising, registrations and licences, exemptions, insurance or security, management plans, return systems, fees, records, agents, stewardship plan approval, consumer-fee prohibitions, and advisory committees.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers for stewardship boards, designated materials, material management registrations, fees, records, agents, plans, consumer-fee rules, and advisory committees.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulation powers for confidentiality, remediation, administrative penalties, forms, service, definitions, transitions, and general protection

evidenceText: respecting the confidentiality of documents and other information
clean-up, site rehabilitation or other remedial action
administrative penalties may be payable
respecting forms for the purposes of this Act and the regulations
providing for any transitional matters
necessary for the protection of the environment

proposedGroups.reason: The closing active paragraphs authorize regulations for confidentiality, remedial-action conditions and orders, administrative penalties and notices, forms, service, definitions, prescribed things, transitional matters, environmental protection, and carrying out the Act's spirit, intent, meaning, and purpose.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers for confidentiality, remedial action, administrative penalties, forms, service, definitions, transitional matters, and general environmental protection.

reason: Section 32.1 is a cohesive incorporation-by-reference provision allowing regulations to incorporate protocols, standards, policies, guidelines, or procedures as amended or fixed, require compliance, and requiring public availability.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Incorporation by reference and public availability
proposedGroups.reason: The two subsections work together by authorizing incorporation by reference in regulations and requiring public access to incorporated materials.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how regulations may incorporate protocols, standards, policies, guidelines, or procedures by reference and what public availability duty follows.
